articleTitle: Using Machine Learning Algorithms in Edge Intelligence for Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Communications in the Industrial Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Given the rapid advancements in technologies such as the metaverse and digital twins, the need for effective integration of communication, computation, and storage in complex systems and edge computing environments is becoming increasingly apparent. This paper proposes an architecture to support an industrial metaverse based on digital twins that optimizes resources by leveraging mobile edge computing and ultra-reliable low-latency communication. This architecture reduces latency by employing task offloading and storage methods on nearby edge servers, meeting the precise requirements of future metaverses in terms of reliability and latency minimization. The proposed model, utilizing reinforcement learning algorithms such as Deep Q-Network (DQN), Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN), and Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (Dueling DDQN), is capable of achieving adaptability in dynamic conditions and making intelligent decisions. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces by more than 10% on average compared to the best method available in the literature and improves resource utilization efficiency.

articleTitle: Locality Preserving Projection Based Autoencoder for Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly detection is a hot topic in remote sensing field. The background reconstruction using various autoencoder based networks have been proposed in recent years where the anomaly map is obtained through difference of the reconstructed background from the hyperspectral image (HSI). Most of anomaly detectors use the original HSI for background estimation through the network. But, in this work, it is proposed that the locality preserving projection (LPP) is used to transform the original feature space. The graph constructed by the randomly selected points through the image with their spectral distances computed as the weights of edges provide a feature space containing the geometrical characteristics and background similarities. The transformed LPP space is used as input of the fully connected autoencoder (AE) and convolutional AE (CAE). The experimental results show detection improvement due to LPP feature space compared to the original HSI while no significant computations are imposed to the detector.

articleTitle: Improving Physical Layer Computation with Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: In this paper, we maximize the computational rate in the physical layer of a multiuser uplink setup using the compute-and-forward method in an environment equipped with Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS). This is achieved by interacting the elements of the RIS with the environment to find the optimal phase angles which best align the effective uplink channel gains with the required linear combination coefficients. For this purpose, the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm, a member of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) cat-egory, is used. Our proposed method improves the performance of the required linear computation by carefully adjusting the phases of RIS elements. To compare the results of the DDPG-based method with previous work in a similar scenario, the Alternating Optimization (AO) approach is also examined. In a typical uplink scenario, it is shown that the performance is improved by 33, 20 and 10 percent (on average) for a setup with 2, 5 and 10 users, respectively. In addition to the above-mentioned performance improvement, another advantage of the proposed DDPG-based algorithm is that it does not require Channel State Information (CSI) being fed back to RIS controller, whereas the alternating optimization method requires.

articleTitle: On the Applicability of the Power Law Signature in the Cyber Security Data
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: The power law distribution is a common statistical phenomenon observed in a wide range of natural and human-made systems including the cybersecurity data such as network and endpoint logs. We analyze the power law distribution of both laboratory and real-world data in cybersecurity. The signature, in most experiments, is in the form of a power law distribution. The tail or head of the power law distribution can show the presence of an attacker depending on the application. In a DDoS attack, the head of the power law distribution shows the probability of an attacker's sending huge traffic. On the other hand, in a threat hunting application, the tail of the distribution shows the probability of the suspicious activity of an attacker that is rare in the network. Furthermore, learning the parameters of the power law distribution, as a new approach, can be embedded in the neural network model to help increase the generalizability of the model as well as out-of-distribution detection. Parameters of this distribution, in the context of the real-world, help understand the structure of the data in real time for attack detection purposes and to define a baseline for detecting an attack or anomaly behavior.

articleTitle: An Improved Hybrid Data Warehousing Architecture for Cloud Service Providers
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Traditional Data Warehouses (DWHs) are inefficient for handling the growing volume, variety, and velocity of modern data. This paper introduces a novel hybrid data warehousing architecture designed for cloud service providers (CSPs), which integrates the strengths of Data Warehouses, Data Lakes, and Data Marts into a unified framework. This innovative architecture enables seamless integration and processing of structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data, addressing the challenges posed by diverse data types in cloud environments. Unlike traditional approaches that treat data processing in isolation, the proposed architecture supports both real-time and batch processing within a single system, improving query performance and facilitating dynamic decision-making. The architecture's flexibility allows it to efficiently manage large datasets and adapt to fluctuating workloads. A key feature of this system is its focus on scalability, security, and real-time analytics, making it particularly suitable for CSPs across service models such as IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. The proposed hybrid repository model significantly enhances data governance and ensures robust data protection. By unifying different data storage models, it optimizes storage management and streamlines data access.

articleTitle: VitaCap: A Vision Transformer-Based Framework for Image Captioning
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Automatic image captioning, which involves generating textual descriptions from visual content, is a challenging and multidisciplinary task combining computer vision and natural language processing. This paper introduces VitaCap (Vision Transformer for Captioning), a transformer-based encoder-decoder architecture designed for effective image caption generation. The model integrates multiple feature extraction technique U-Net [1] for pixel features, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) [2] for grid features, and Faster R-CNN [3] for region-based features providing a rich and comprehensive visual representation. These features are processed by the transformer encoder to capture complex dependencies, which are then utilized by the decoder to generate meaningful and contextually relevant captions. Experimental results demonstrate that VitaCap achieves promising performance across various image datasets, highlighting its potential as a robust solution for image captioning tasks.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Mathematical Proficiency of Large Language Models in Computer Science Graduate Admission Tests
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of six prominent Large Language Models (LLMs) on graduate entrance exam multiple-choice mathematics questions in computer science, computer engineering, and information technology programs, with a focus on their cross-lingual capabilities. The selected models, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.1 405B, Mistral Large 2, and Qwen 2.5 72B, were tested on 146 questions presented in both Persian and English, spanning four key mathematical domains. Results reveal significant variations in accuracy, with Gemini 1.5 Pro achieving the highest overall performance in English (63.70%) and Claude 3.5 leading in Persian (52.0%). However, some models struggled with maintaining consistent accuracy across languages, showing a cross-lingual performance gap. The findings underscore the potential of LLMs in addressing complex mathematical tasks but also highlight their current limitations, particularly in multilingual contexts. Notable disparities in model performance point to the importance of architectural innovations and multilingual training.

articleTitle: Motion-Based Human Spatial Problem-Solving Assessment Using Hand Movement Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Spatial problem-solving is a cognitive process involving the identification, analysis, and resolution of challenges through mental strategies and critical thinking. This skill is essential for manipulating objects and solving complex spatial tasks. Insufficient problem-solving ability can lead to difficulties in decision-making, adaptability, and professional growth in spatial reasoning. This study aims to develop an index correlating with Mental Rotation Test (MRT) scores, inspired by traditional assessments and hand movement tracking data. Twenty-six participants took part in this study and initially completed a paper-based MRT. They then viewed a 3D shape from three perspectives on a monitor and constructed a matching model using cubes, while a camera-based real-time hand tracking system recorded hand key point coordinates. Predictors were developed by analyzing hand movement distance and time-based measures during the tasks. The proposed index achieved an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0. 7 and a mean absolute error of 2.32. This dynamic assessment method can potentially provide a faster, more cost-efficient, and detailed evaluation of human spatial problem-solving skills.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Chunk Time on Video Streaming Performance in TCP-Based Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: The exponential increase in video traffic on the Internet has generated a heightened demand for efficient video streaming solutions. HTTP Adaptive Streaming (HAS) has emerged as a viable strategy, facilitating dynamic quality adaptation in response to fluctuating network conditions. In HAS, media content is segmented into short time intervals, with each segment encoded in multiple bitrate-resolution combinations known as representations. This framework enables users to choose the most appropriate representation according to their current network connectivity. To enhance the selection of bit rates and elevate the Quality of Experience (QoE), it is crucial to conduct a precise assessment of network conditions. This research investigated the impact of chunk time on video streaming performance in TCP-based networks. Analyzing the effects of chunk time on both QoE and throughput, our findings indicate that similar to the adaptive nature of video representations that depend on network conditions, chunk time must also be adaptive. It is essential that the chunk time is tailored to the specific network environment, necessitating an adaptive chunk-time strategy for each resolution to ensure optimal streaming performance.

articleTitle: Quantifying Heterogeneity of Complex Networks Based on Gintropy and Gini Indices
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Characterizing the heterogeneity of complex networks is a fundamental challenge in studying complex networks. Most of the proposed measures are vertex-degree based, falling short of capturing essential characteristic features of heterogeneous networks. The Gini index is an inequality measure extensively used in economics and the social sciences and Gintropy is a newly proposed inequality measure based on the Gini index. In this paper, we use Gintropy to characterize the heterogeneity of complex networks. Our experimental results show that Gintropy can be effectively used as a heterogeneity index. The benefit of adopting Gintropy as a heterogeneity index is that it accurately quantifies the rich club graph as the most heterogeneous graph.

articleTitle: Effective Preprocessing and Explainability for Better Lung Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in the medical field has expanded significantly in recent years. Among its various subsets, machine learning (ML) demonstrates immense potential for enhancing the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. In this study, we aim to enhance the classification outcomes of recent lung cancer research by effective preprocessing techniques and emphasizing the impact of features derived from the ‘Survey Lung Cancer’ dataset. To improve classifier performance, different tasks such as SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) for handling class imbalance and MinMaxScaler for feature scaling, were applied. These preprocessing steps significantly enhanced model accuracy. Specifically, the SVM classifier achieved a PR AUC of 99%, while the Random Forest (RF) classifier demonstrated the best performance across other evaluation metrics, achieving an accuracy of 97.91 %. Additionally, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) were employed to identify the most influential features contributing to each model's predictions. These techniques helped identify the most influential features contributing to each model's predictions, enhancing interpretability and understanding of their outputs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Proof-of-Work Blockchain Network Communications Using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Proof-of-Work (PoW) blockchains are a fundamental component of decentralized systems, ensuring security and consensus through computational processes. However, their widespread adoption has highlighted critical challenges, including excessive communication overhead and resource consumption, which can hinder scalability and operational efficiency. This study tackles these issues by optimizing network topologies in PoW blockchains using advanced tool. Through the application of a genetic algorithm, we systematically generate and refine network configurations to minimize communication costs, measured by the total data exchanged during essential operations such as transaction propagation and block dissemination. By carefully balancing node placement and router connections, our approach successfully reduces overall data traffic. The results indicate a remarkable optimization rate of 20.2 %, underscoring the effectiveness of genetic algorithm in enhancing PoW blockchain efficiency without compromising core functionalities. This research offers a practical path forward for designing scalable blockchain systems, particularly in environments with constrained resources.

articleTitle: A Double Approximate Neural Hardware Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Emerging as a prominent approach, approximate computing has found widespread application in diverse fields such as data mining and image processing, effectively curbing area and power consumption in processors. One compelling avenue for integrating approximate computing involves the integration of a neural accelerator alongside the primary core, offering a delicate balance between computational efficiency and precision. A Neural Processing Unit (NPU) emulates regions of approximate code using neural networks. In this article, we introduce ANPiler- an innovative framework that augments the existing neural processing unit with a reconfigurable layer of approximation, achieved through the integration of inexact arithmetic building blocks. ANPiler empowers the design of neural accelerators featuring imprecise adders or multipliers, resulting in reductions of about S.55% in power consumption and approximately 13.09% in area compared to a precise neural processing unit coupled with a main core. These gains are achieved with almost the same accuracy as before, further underpinning energy savings of 3.0x compared to general-purpose processors, thereby reinforcing the value proposition of an exact NPU in practical applications.

articleTitle: Finding the Sweet Spot: An Empirical Study on Dataset Size, Performance, and Efficiency in Relation Extraction
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Relation extraction (RE) is a critical task in natural language processing that identifies relationships between entities within text. While increasing the size of annotated datasets generally enhances model performance, the cost and effort associated with human annotation can be prohibitive. This study investigates the impact of dataset size on RE performance using the Semantic Evaluation 2010 Task 8 dataset. Four deep neural models-Attention-Based Convolutional Neural Network, Attention-Based Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Network, Relation Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, and Matching the Blanks-were evaluated across eight subsets of the dataset to simulate size reduction. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were analyzed. The results indicate that although larger datasets improve model performance, the benefits diminish beyond a certain size, illustrating the law of diminishing returns. These findings emphasize the importance of balancing dataset size and quality for cost-effective training and suggest strategies such as data augmentation and transfer learning to optimize performance with limited data.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on SALSA-Lite Method for Localization of Multiple Human Speakers
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: SALSA-Lite is a fast and efficient feature designed for localization and detection of polyphonic sound events (SELD) with microphone array inputs. It serves as a lightweight version of the original SALSA feature for polyphonic SELD. In this paper, we specifically use a SELD network based on SALSA-Lite features to localize sound events from multiple human female/male speakers. We have conducted a series of experiments to evaluate its effectiveness in determining Direction of Arrival (DoA) solely based on auditory events derived from speech. While the base method's superior performance regarding complexity and accuracy has been established in the localization of sound events relative to leading methodologies, we show that it encounters additional difficulties when speech sources are in close proximity to one another, particularly when noise and reverberation significantly obscure speech signals. We also demonstrate that the number of active speakers, their distances from the microphone array, and their tone of voice can significantly impact the performance of SELD network based on SALSA-Lite features.

articleTitle: Geometric Autoencoder with Manifold Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Autoencoders are widely recognized as non-probabilistic learning models for extracting useful information from data. Most autoencoder models assume a Euclidean geometry for the underlying nature of the data. However, recent advancements in geometric learning suggest that incorporating curvature information of the intrinsic manifold of data may yield richer representations. In this work, we investigate the performance of a learning method that embeds data under curved geometric constraints. Our method assumes that the data manifold consists of both curved and Euclidean spaces. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art techniques

articleTitle: FeAdaBoost: Enhancing Federated Learning Accuracy by Ensemble Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL), an advanced technique in machine learning (ML), allows for model training without transferring data to a central server. This method is particularly valuable in sensitive applications, such as healthcare and finance, as it preserves data privacy and reduces security risks. However, FL faces the challenge of reduced accuracy compared to centralized approaches due to limited access to the full dataset. To address this issue, we propose a solution that integrates the ensemble learning method AdaBoost with FL, which we call FeAdaBoost. We validate the effectiveness of our approach using the task of classifying a chest X-ray image dataset. The experimental results confirm that the proposed approach significantly improves both accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional FL.

articleTitle: Low-Level Feature Representation in the RCSU-Net Model Using Channel-Spatial Attention Mechanism for Semantic Segmentation of Plant Leaves
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Smart agriculture leverages advanced technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT), deep learning, and computer vision to address challenges in plant disease detection and management. Semantic image segmentation has become an essential tool for monitoring plant health by detecting subtle anomalies and patterns through visual data analysis. While encoder-decoder architectures such as U-Net show great potential, they face challenges like the loss of low-level features, incomplete texture analysis, and weak edge detection, which limit segmentation accuracy. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an enhanced U-Net model that integrates ResNet-50 as the encoder and incorporates a channel-spatial attention block in the decoder. This architecture preserves low-level features like edges and textures, enabling precise segmentation of diseased regions in plant leaves. Experimental results demonstrate the model's effectiveness, achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.35% and a Dice coefficient of 96.45%, indicating its superior performance. These advancements highlight the model's significant potential for real-world applications in disease detection and efficient crop management. The code for this research is publicly available at https://github.com/Faphnut/Plant-Disease-semantic-segmentation.git

articleTitle: Zero Memory Overhead Approach for Protecting Vision Transformer Parameters Against Bit-Flip Faults
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViT<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>) have demonstrated superior performance over Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in various vision-related tasks such as classification, object detection, and segmentation due to their use of self-attention mechanisms. As ViTs become more popular in safety-critical applications like autonomous driving, ensuring their correct functionality becomes essential, especially in the presence of bit-flip faults in their parameters stored in memory. In this paper, a fault tolerance technique is introduced to protect ViT parameters against bit-flip faults with zero memory overhead. Since the least significant bits of parameters are not critical for model accuracy, replacing the LSB with a parity bit provides an error detection mechanism without imposing any overhead on the model. When faults are detected, affected parameters are masked by zeroing out, as most parameters in ViT models are near zero, effectively preventing accuracy degradation. This approach enhances reliability across ViT models, improving the robustness of parameters to bit-flips by up to three orders of magnitude, making it an effective zero-overhead solution for fault tolerance in critical applications.

articleTitle: Persian Physical Activity Recommender System Based on ParsBERT
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Engaging in regular exercise is essential for maintaining health and preventing various chronic diseases. However, many individuals fail to meet the recommended levels of exercise due to barriers such as a lack of time, motivation, or access to facilities. Consequently, developing personalized and effective interventions to encourage exercise presents a significant challenge. In this paper, we propose a novel Persian exercise recommender system based on ParsBERT, a state-of-the-art language model for Persian natural language processing. The proposed system aims to provide tailored and timely suggestions for exercise to users based on their preferences. It utilizes ParsBERT to understand users' natural language inputs and recommend suitable sports videos. Additionally, it leverages ParsBERT to learn from users' behaviors and preferences over time, adapting its recommendations accordingly. We evaluate our system using a dataset of 100 Persian-speaking users who interacted with the platform. We measure its effectiveness in terms of adherence to exercise recommendations. Furthermore, we compare it with several baseline systems that do not utilize ParsBERT. The results indicate that our system outperforms the baseline systems across all metrics, demonstrating the potential of using ParsBERT to develop intelligent and personalized exercise recommender systems for Persian speakers.

articleTitle: Detecting Vulnerable Smart Contracts by Security Risk Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Detecting vulnerable smart contracts has a direct effect on blockchain security because it helps users avoid using these contracts. In this study, the problem of vulnerability risk for blockchain smart contracts is introduced. Moreover, an effective criterion for its estimation is devised. With this criterion, to estimate the risk of an unknown smart contract, linear discriminant analysis of smart contracts and distances to their nearest neighbors were exploited. Although deep learning is not used in the proposed criterion and it requires little training data, it provides a realistic risk estimation of smart contracts. The experiments conducted on a real-world dataset of Ethereum blockchain smart contracts, including both vulnerable and safe contracts, show the acceptable performance of the proposed criterion. Moreover, the performance of the proposed criterion is superior to that of existing criteria in other areas of risk estimation.

articleTitle: Cluster Aware Personalized News Recommendation System Using a Global News Graph
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: With the increasing use of online news services and the production of a large amount of news daily, finding news content that matches user interests has become an important challenge. Personalized news recommendation systems, by mod-eling users' behavior and interests, can help us to respond to this challenge. In this study, a new method for personalized news recommendations based on clustering and graph enhancement has been introduced, consisting of two primary phases. The first phase involves dividing the news graph into multiple clusters. In the second phase, recommendations are generated within each cluster. The findings indicate that this proposed approach yields more precise recommendations while also reducing computational demands.

articleTitle: AcDWS:Actor Based Distributed Web Scraping
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This paper examines a new system for web data extraction that utilizes an AcDWS approach. The main goal of this system is to collect information related to user-requested products quickly and at scale. In this system, communication between actors is managed, and the messages exchanged between them are controlled to ensure proper operation. Solr is used for data storage and full-text search, Akka for parallel processing, and Akka Cluster for distributed processing. The results show that this method operates 75% faster than conventional methods using Python and 36.7% faster than data extraction implemented in Java sequentially.

articleTitle: Optimized Multi-Label Human Activity Recognition with Focal Loss and Attention-Enhanced LSTM Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Recognizing human activity using artificial intelligence and deep learning methods has become increasingly important in various fields, including medicine, sports, security, and wearable technology. With the rise of data collection tools that utilize multidimensional sensors and the growing need for faster and more accurate analysis of human behaviors, deep neural networks can potentially improve traditional approaches, enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of activity detection systems. This research, which leverages deep learning and neural networks in the arena of human activity detection, plays a significant role in the advancement of sensor data and time series analysis models. Previous studies often converted time series data into structured formats; however, these methods mainly struggled with accuracy and efficiency in representing and analyzing complex features, which limited their practical applications. The current research aims to address this gap by focusing on deep neural network models. These models excel in processing multidimensional data and learning complex features, making them better suited for recognizing and classifying human behaviors.

articleTitle: Approximate Full-Adder, Full-Subtractor, and Full-Adder/Subtractor Circuits Based on QCA
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: QCA has garnered a lot of attention lately because to its promise for low latency, compact space, low complexity, and low power consumption. At the same time, a new nanotechnology paradigm called approximation computing simplifies computation high-performance design method, and becomes a low-power for calculation circuits. Additionally, a lot of digital circuit design has made use of the XOR gate. A crucial part of QCA technology, the full-adder (FA) circuit is used for arithmetic logic unit operations such as subtraction, multiplication, and division. The design of approximation FA, full-subtractor (FS), and full-adder/subtractor (F<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>/S) has been extensively studied. The approximate F<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>/S designs demonstrated just 10 cells utilized in implementation, an area of 0.01μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and a delay of 0.5 clock phases. Specifically, the approximate FA and FS designs achieved an area of 0.01 μm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and a latency of 0.5 clock phases. By using the QCADesigner tool for functional verification, the efficacy of these designs was confirmed. Three new and innovative QCA-based circuits-FA/S, FS, and FA approximations-are presented in this work. Accessing the components without being surrounded by other cells is made easy by the fact that each design has outputs on one side and the inputs on the other side.

articleTitle: PTSA: Utilizing Transaction Prioritization to Enhance Confirmation Speed in the IOTA Network
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of blockchain technology, a significant trend is the adoption of Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) as an alternative to traditional chain-based architectures for organizing ledger records. Systems like IOTA, which are specially designed for the Internet of Things (Io'T), leverage DAG-based architectures to achieve greater scalability by enabling multiple attachment points in the ledger for new transactions while allowing these transactions to be added to the network without incurring any fees. To determine these attachment points, many tip selection algorithms commonly employ specific strategies on the DAG ledger. Transaction prioritization is not considered in the IOTA network, which becomes especially important when network bandwidth is limited. In this paper, we propose an optimization framework designed to integrate a priority level for critical or high-priority IoT transactions within the IOTA network. We evaluate our system using fully based on the official IOTA GitHub repository, which employs the currently operational IOTA node software (Hornet version), as part of the Chrysalis update (1.5). The experimental results show that higher-priority transactions in the proposed algorithm reach final confirmation in less time compared to the original IOTA system.

articleTitle: Predicting NBA Playoffs Qualification Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Sports data analysis has become an essential aspect of modern sports management, leveraging machine learning (ML) techniques to gain valuable insights into team and player performance. This study proposes a novel ML-based framework to predict NBA teams' qualification for the playoffs, utilizing comprehensive per-game data from the 2013–2014 to 2023–2024 seasons. Key features were selected using SHAP analysis, and model performance was evaluated using a rigorous 5-fold cross-validation approach. Among the models tested, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved the highest prediction accuracy (96%), followed by the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) with an 88% accuracy. These results highlight the potential of ML in providing actionable insights for team owners, coaches, and stakeholders to make data-driven decisions. Furthermore, the study addresses challenges such as data imbalance and provides a comparative analysis of model performance, offering a valuable contribution to the growing field of sports analytics

articleTitle: Intelligent Resource Allocation in IoT: An ACO-GA Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices demands efficient resource allocation to optimize utilization and minimize communication overhead. This research introduces a novel hybrid approach that combines Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) to optimize resource allocation in IoT environments. The primary goal is to enhance network performance and reduce communication costs between IoT devices and gateways. Our hybrid approach leverages the strengths of ACO in finding optimal paths and GA's local search capabilities for fine-tuning, resulting in a robust and reliable solution for resource allocation in complex IoT settings. Comparative analysis, based on various benchmarks, demonstrates that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing resource allocation techniques, achieving substantial reductions in total communication costs. The results highlight the effectiveness of the hybrid ACO-GA approach for efficient resource management in IoT networks.

articleTitle: ELEMENT: Energy and Latency Management with Reinforcement Learning-Based Offloading in Vehicular Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: With the recent advancements in smart vehicles and ever-increasing tasks that need to be processed, Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) emerged as a promising solution. Smart vehicles have numerous tasks and their local processing power is insufficient to process all of them. Offloading the tasks to edge servers and utilizing the processing power of those servers is a decent solution to solving this problem. Still, the decision-making for offloading is challenging due to the delay and energy con-sumption caused by transmitting data which significantly impacts two crucial parameters of a VEC environment: latency and the energy consumption of the smart vehicle. Energy and latency are closely related, and a low-latency system consumes more power, while a low-energy system has higher latencies. The balancing challenge of these two has become a popular research area with many contributions. In this paper, we propose a Reinforcement Learning (RL) approach for taking the offloading decision to find a balance between latency and the consumed energy. Utilizing RL, allowed our method to be flexible and adaptive to diverse scenarios, especially in large-scale and dynamic environments. By conducting realistic simulations using SUMO standard we gained up to 18.35% improvement in average response time while reducing energy consumption up to 5 % compared to other baselines.

articleTitle: ZharfSima: Benchmarking Vision Language Models for Persian Language and Culture
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This literature presents ZharfSima. the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) tailored to the Persian language and Iranian cultural contexts. The benchmark includes datasets for reasoning, Iranian cultural knowledge, standard and text generation, featuring tasks like driving test questions, IQ problems, and cultural assessments. Key contributions include the introduction of the Persian SEED benchmark and unique datasets like NaarDoon, designed for evaluating cultural and visual reasoning. By utilizing ZharfSima benchmark, we compared the performance of open-source VLMs (Qwen2- VL, Llama-3.2-Vision, NVLM-D) and GPT-40 on classification and text generation tasks. Results show GPT-40 excels in cultural understanding and text generation, achieving over 70% accuracy in Iranian Essence task, while Qwen2- VL performs best among open models. However, reasoning tasks remain challenging for all models, with performance under 30%. This work highlights the need for improved VLM training on low-resource languages like Persian and the impact of instruction's language on performance, where English questions outperform Persian ones. This benchmark serves as a critical resource for advancing multimodal AI in underrepresented languages.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Delay-Optimized Task Offloading in Vehicular Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: The imminent rise of Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) is revolutionizing the future of transport. The Vehicular Fog Computing (VFC) paradigm has emerged to alleviate the load of compute-intensive and delay-sensitive AV programs via task of-floading to nearby vehicles. Effective VFC requires an intelligent and dynamic offloading algorithm. As a result, this paper adapts Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) for VFC offloading. First, a simulation environment utilizing realistic hardware and task specifications, in addition to a novel vehicular movement model based on grid-planned cities, is created. Afterward, a DRL-based algorithm is trained and tested on the environment with the goal of minimizing global task delay. The DRL model displays impressive results, outperforming other greedy and conventional methods. The findings further demonstrate the effectiveness of the DRL model in minimizing queue congestion, especially when compared to traditional cloud computing methods that struggle to handle the demands of a large fleet of vehicles. This is corroborated by queuing theory, highlighting the self-scalability of the VFC-based DRL approach.

articleTitle: Adaptive Chunking for VideoRAG Pipelines with a Newly Gathered Bilingual Educational Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for video question answering (VideoQA) through the development of an adaptive chunking methodology and the creation of a bilingual educational dataset. Our proposed adaptive chunking technique, powered by CLIP embeddings and SSIM scores, identifies meaningful transitions in video content by segmenting educational videos into semantically coherent chunks. This methodology optimizes the processing of slide-based lectures, ensuring efficient integration of visual and textual modalities for downstream RAG tasks. To support this work, we gathered a bilingual dataset comprising Persian and English mid- to long-duration academic videos, curated to reflect diverse topics, teaching styles, and multilingual content. Each video is enriched with synthetic question-answer pairs designed to challenge pure large language models (LLMs) and underscore the necessity of retrieval-augmented systems. The evaluation compares our CLIP-SSIM-based chunking approach against conventional video slicing methods, demonstrating significant improvements across RAGAS metrics, including Answer Relevance, Context Relevance, and Faithfulness. Fur-thermore, our findings reveal that the multimodal image-text retrieval scenario achieves the best overall performance, emphasizing the importance of integrating complementary modalities. articleTitle: TIS: Three-Tiered Intelligent Supply Chain Management to Enhance Quality and Supervision
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Efficient supplier management and collaboration with top-tier suppliers are crucial for maintaining competitiveness in today's automotive industry, where competition is fierce, and globalization presents both challenges and opportunities. This study introduces an innovative approach that harnesses artificial intelligence with the aim of Digital Transformation and implements Industry 4.0 for the automotive industry to improve supply chain operations by establishing a tiered and hierarchical system. The proposed approach helps minimize errors, prevent fraud, and enhance product quality in this industry. The methodology involves extracting key features from supplier data, applying the K-means algorithm for clustering, and implementing a hierarchical system for efficient supplier management. Furthermore, techniques like Gartner Magic Quadrant charts are incorporated to increase understanding and support decisions for company experts to overcome challenges and enhance decision-making in selecting and contracting with stable suppliers. We can consolidate our suppliers to a small number of delegates to represent suppliers per system, reducing our contracts by 84.33% - 92.17% and improving operational efficiency by using this system in the company of this case study. Moreover, by reducing the number of unique parts by 99.66%, we aim to simplify logistics, optimize supply chain operations, and improve inventory management. Additionally, implementing this intelligent system can reduce the workforce directly involved in these operations by 93.290/0 and save 39,180,000 person-hours over 20 years. The results show that this approach effectively categorizes suppliers, highlights key evaluation criteria, and supports decision-making processes. Ultimately, this leads to a more efficient supply chain, improved overall performance, and increased company revenue.

articleTitle: ARGENT: Energy-Aware Scheduling in Edge Computing Using Energy Valley Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for energy-aware task scheduling in heterogeneous edge computing environments. The Energy Valley Optimizer (EVO) is exploited for the optimal allocation of tasks to edge devices with limited resources. The primary objective of this algorithm is to minimize energy consumption and task completion time while achieving optimal resource utilization. The EVO updates task positions in the search space using our proposed alpha, beta, and gamma reduction processes, avoiding local optima. Our evaluations on both small and large scales with real-world datasets indicate that our approach reduces energy consumption by an average of 14.42 %, reaching up to 20.96% savings, and decreases task completion time by an average of 15.98%, with a peak improvement of 24.42%, in comparison to state-of-the-art methods. Additionally, EVO shows a 5.28% improvement in success ratio, which means it is robust in meeting task deadlines.

articleTitle: RADTO: A Resource-Aware and Dynamic Task Offloading Strategy for Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: With the rapid evolution of technology, the demand for mobile devices capable of executing computationally intensive and time-sensitive applications has surged. However, these devices are often constrained by limited storage, finite battery life, and insufficient processing power, making it difficult to meet such demands effectively. Task offloading, which involves transferring computational tasks to more capable infrastructures, has emerged as a promising solution to these challenges. In this paper, we propose a novel task offloading strategy based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) that dynamically accounts for the computational capacities of both user devices and servers. This approach aims to optimize execution time while adhering to energy consumption and bandwidth limitations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy outperforms existing methods, achieving significantly lower execution times without violating energy and bandwidth constraints. Furthermore, the strategy incorporates partial offloading capabilities to enhance flexibility and maximize resource utilization.

articleTitle: DNA Computing: A Breakthrough in Image Cryptography - A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Deoxyribonucleic acid-DNA computing, an interdisciplinary field at the frontier between molecular biology and computer science, has become a revolutionary field. DNA computation provides a new approach to data computation and cryptography. The inherent properties of DNA include high parallelism, excellent data density, and stability; it can hence be considered one of the ideal candidates in cryptographic applications, especially in image encryption. This review provides recent advances in DNA-based cryptographic algorithms, their fusion with chaotic systems, and also their applications to practical scenarios that enhance data security. Different algorithms are studied that exploit the encoding capability of DNA, such as substitution, transposition, and hybrid models including crossover and mutation. It also discusses DNA for secure image transmission in applications like healthcare, industrial IoT, and cloud environments. The latter presents scalability challenges and problems regarding key generation along with certain implementation constraints, while at the same time pointing future research toward a perspective of opening up for stronger cryptography.

articleTitle: Optimizing Location Allocation in Urban Management: A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Various issues in the fields of urban management, digital transformation, and smart cities have been presented recently. Currently, we like to attend to optimizing location allocation problems that can be a new part of digital transformation in urban management (such as locating and placing facilities, locating and arranging centers such as aid and rescue centers, or even postal hubs, telecommunications, electronic equipment, data centers, and routing in transportation optimization). These issues, which are seemingly simple but in practice complex, are important in urban environments, and the issue of accurate location allocation based on existing criteria directly impacts cost management, profit, efficiency, and citizen satisfaction. In recent years, researchers have used or presented various models and methods for location allocation problems, some of which will be mentioned in this article. This review examines heuristic and meta-heuristic approaches, including GA, PSO, and GIS-based models, highlighting their applications and limitations in urban management optimization. Finally, a brief conclusion will be made of the existing methods and some of their weaknesses, and suggestions will be made for continuing the path and improving scientific and practical research in this field.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning: A Hyperledger Fabric Approach for Secure IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: The rapid growth of loT devices necessitates robust solutions to ensure data privacy and security in distributed learning environments. This paper proposes a novel frame-work combining federated learning with Hyperledger Fabric blockchain to enable decentralized model training while safe-guarding sensitive data. By leveraging blockchain's immutability and auditability alongside federated learning's data localization, the system establishes a secure and transparent ecosystem for collaborative machine learning. The paper details the system architecture, implementation strategies, and integration chal-lenges, offering a practical solution for secure, privacy-preserving learning in loT environments and highlighting the potential of blockchain-enabled federated learning for decentralized, data-sensitive applications.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Greedy Task Offloading Algorithm for Vehicular Edge Computing Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Modern vehicles require a significant processing power along with storage space. To address this need, offloading the vehicular tasks to adjacent edge servers has been proposed. However, even the considerable processing power of edge servers may not be sufficient to cope with the increasing demand of vehicular computational tasks, leading to potential failure to complete tasks within their deadlines. Vehicular Edge Computing (VEC) has emerged as a promising approach to provide these necessary computational and storage needs through powerful edge servers together with the resources of the nearby vehicles, whereby improving latency for delay-sensitive tasks. However, this heterogeneous processing environment requires a suitable task offloading and scheduling mechanism. This paper introduces a lightweight greedy task offloading algorithm, addressing this requirement by considering the possibility of collaboration between edge servers and utilizing the idle resources of parked vehicles within the edge servers' coverage area. A system solution for efficient use of resources in vehicles and edge servers will be presented. The task offloading problem is modeled as an optimization problem with the objective of maximizing the task completion ratio (TCR), which will be solved using a two-layer greedy approach. Simulation results demonstrate that, on average, the proposed task offloading method can improve the TCR by a factor of 1.29.

articleTitle: MPEC: Manifold-Preserved EEG Classification via an Ensemble of Clustering-Based Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Accurate classification of EEG signals is crucial for brain-computer interfaces (BCls) and neuroprosthetic applications, yet many existing methods fail to account for the non-Euclidean, manifold structure of EEG data, resulting in suboptimal performance. Preserving this manifold information is essential to capture the true geometry of EEG signals, but traditional classification techniques largely overlook this need. To this end, we propose MPEC (Manifold-Preserved EEG Classification via an Ensemble of Clustering-Based Classifiers), that introduces two key innovations: (1) a feature engineering phase that combines covariance matrices and Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels to capture both linear and non-linear relationships among EEG channels, and (2) a clustering phase that employs a modified K-means algorithm tailored for the Riemannian manifold space, ensuring local geometric sensitivity. Ensembling multiple clustering-based classifiers, MPEC achieves superior results, validated by significant improvements on the BCI Competition IV dataset 2a.

articleTitle: Node Embedding Extraction for Causal Brain Graphs in fMRI Data
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This study introduces a novel pipeline for feature extraction from Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) data, focusing on age-related trends in node embeddings derived from causal brain graphs during naturalistic stimuli (movie observation). Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) constructed using the Non-combinatorial Optimization via Trace Exponential and Augmented Lagrangian for Structure learning (NOTEARS) algorithm modeled causal relationships among 25 brain regions of interest (ROIs). Graph embeddings were generated using the Deep Walk algorithm to capture low-dimensional representations of graph structures. Unlike previous studies analyzing functional brain graphs with traditional graph metrics (e.g., degree, centrality, clustering coefficient), our approach employs modern techniques to uncover patterns in effective brain graphs. The results revealed decreasing feature similarity with age in regions associated with Theory of Mind (ToM), Pain, Face and Place Processing, reflecting age-related neural changes. Conversely, the Left Retrosplenial Cortex (IRSC) demonstrated increasing similarity, suggesting enhanced maturation and efficiency in spatial memory functions. Regions like the Left Fusiform Face Area (IFF A) and Right Transverse Occipital Sulcus (rTOS) showed no significant trends, emphasizing the role of functional relevance in brain responses to naturalistic stimuli. The novelty of our research lies in analyzing localized patterns in causal brain graphs using embedding techniques like Deep Walk, moving beyond traditional metrics. For the first time, features were extracted from fMRI data to study node-level similarities across age groups during naturalistic stimuli. By combining effective graph construction with localized embedding methods, this pipeline advances age-related brain connectivity research, demonstrating the consistent impact of movie stimuli on brain dynamics and the potential of graph-based methods to reveal age-related neural connectivity changes.

articleTitle: A Novel Mixed-Method Approach to Missing Value Imputation: An Introduction to MissMixed
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Handling missing data is a pervasive challenge in machine learning and statistical analysis, often leading to biased models and reduced accuracy if not properly addressed. Numerous imputation algorithms have been proposed, ranging from simple statistical methods to complex machine learning models. In this paper, we introduce MissMixed, an innovative approach to the imputation problem that combines flexibility with robust performance. Unlike conventional imputation algorithms, MissMixed enables the dynamic selection of imputation algorithms and corresponding hyperparameters at each iteration, allowing it to adapt to a dataset's unique structure and missingness patterns. While the default configuration employs Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Tree models, MissMixed's modular design accommodates various machine learning algorithms and parameter settings, similar to the customizable layers in deep learning architectures. To evaluate MissMixed, we conducted extensive experiments on five diverse datasets, including the Breast Cancer Wisconsin and Letter Recognition datasets, with different missing rates and under various missingness mechanisms. We tested MissMixed alongside some of well-established methods, such as MissForest, MICE, KNN, and Variational Autoencoders (VAE), as well as simpler statistical imputation methods. The results reveal that MissMixed consistently achieves high accuracy and, in most scenarios, outperforms other methods. Its adaptability across various conditions underscores MissMixed”s potential as a powerful, versatile imputation approach suited to real-world applications.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attacks and Defense Mechanisms in Spiking Neural Networks: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), often referred to as third-generation neural networks, are inspired by the workings of the human brain and are celebrated for their energy efficiency, positioning them as a promising alternative to traditional Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). However, SNNs face significant challenges in robustness, particularly under adversarial attacks, which can undermine their performance in real-world applications. This survey provides a detailed examination of adversarial attacks targeting SNNs, categorizing existing attack methods and defense mechanisms while highlighting inherent structural characteristics and training approaches that influence robustness. Unlike prior surveys that focus primarily on adversarial attacks in traditional ANNs, this work is the first to consolidate and critically analyze adversarial strategies and defenses specific to SNNs. Furthermore, we quantitatively compare SNNs with ANNs in terms of their susceptibility to adversarial attacks, offering new insights into the unique challenges and opportunities presented by SNNs. These contributions establish this survey as a foundational reference for advancing robust SNN research and development.

articleTitle: POOLER: A No-Code Platform to Automatically Generate Analytical Polls
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: The advancements in technology and widespread internet access have revolutionized the way data collection and polling are conducted. Traditional polling methods are often hampered by significant challenges, including high operational costs, limited ability to reach a broad audience, reliance on a large workforce, and the extensive time required for data analysis. These limitations have led to inefficiencies and reduced the effectiveness of traditional approaches. In this paper, we introduce a platform designed to automate the creation of online polls, utilizing a model-driven approach and no-code development platform. This system streamlines the polling process by allowing users to easily design and deploy polls without extensive programming knowledge. The platform also includes built-in functionalities to automatically generate charts and visualizations for data analysis, reducing the need for manual data processing. By simplifying these processes, the platform makes advanced polling tools accessible to non-experts, enabling quicker, more efficient data collection and analysis in a variety of contexts.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Investigation into Automated Model Transformation Using Q-Learning: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) emphasizes models as primary artifacts to enhance abstraction and automation in software development. However, manually defining model transformation rules is a time-consuming and error-prone task. This study proposes a Q-learning-based approach for automating model transformations by example, where transformation rules are dynamically learned through interaction with paired example models using reinforcement learning. The evaluation of the proposed method on UML-to-Java transformations demonstrates improvements in accuracy and scalability while reducing manual effort. The approach effectively addresses challenges such as model heterogeneities and dependency on high-quality examples, showcasing its potential to streamline and optimize model transformation processes.

articleTitle: Proposing a Novel Approach Based on GAN Neural Networks to Address Data Poisoning Attacks in Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Data poisoning attacks are one of the serious threats in federated learning, which can disrupt the performance of the central model by inj ecting poisoned data into local nodes. These attacks are particularly significant in cloud environments, where distributed and decentralized data are often managed, due to the increasing need for data security. Identifying and isolating poisoned data from clean data in local nodes is a fundamental step toward enhancing the security and stability of these systems. In this paper, a method based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) is proposed, which can act as an effective tool for identifying poisoned samples. In the proposed method, the GAN discriminator's task shifts from solving a binary problem, as is standard in GANs, to identifying the true label of data in a multi-class problem. During the GAN training phase, the semantic information of the data, including the true labels, is incorporated into the discriminator. To evaluate the proposed method, experiments were conducted on the standard MNIST dataset. Compared to standard GANs, the proposed method showed better performance for classes where label-flipping data poisoning was applied. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method in various federated learning environments. The presented method can be used as a solution to enhance the security of data and models in federated learning and to identify the true labels of data in cases where there is no prior information about the occurrence of an attack.

articleTitle: Multi-channel Lung Sound Analysis for COPD Diagnosis Using Statistical Test and Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), known as the most prevalent chronic lung disease, is associated with high global morbidity and mortality rates. This study included 21 participants with lung sounds recorded from their 16 posterior chest locations. The study was conducted in two phases: In the initial phase, statistical tests were employed to analyze the normalized energy of various frequency sub-bands within lung sounds to determine the frequency ranges that best differentiate healthy and COPD groups. Meanwhile, the second phase aimed to assess the diagnostic capabilities of four distinct lung regions and the 16 recording channels using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network. To achieve this, lung sounds were divided into four groups, each representing a specific lung region. Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) were then extracted from these groups, and the performance of both the four lung regions and the initial 16 channels was evaluated using the MLP. Additionally, inspiratory and expiratory phases, as well as complete respiratory cycles, of lung sounds were independently analyzed to determine their discriminative abilities in both study phases. Statistical analysis revealed significant differences between groups across most channels within specific frequency ranges: 200–300 Hz during full respiratory cycle, 200–300 Hz and 500–600 Hz during inspiration, and 600–1000 Hz during expiration. Furthermore, according to the neural network analysis, the upper right lung region and channel 9 demonstrated superior performance, achieving accuracies of 94.3% for complete respiratory cycles and 97.99% for expiration, respectively.

articleTitle: A Context-Aware Attention-Based Model for Enhanced Long Term Traffic Prediction on Non-Graph-Structured Data
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Traffic forecasting remains a critical component in urban traffic management, especially as cities face unprecedented growth and increasing vehicle loads. Although graph-based models have demonstrated strong performance in traffic forecasting, they are not applicable when dealing with limited, non-graph-structured data. In this study, the goal is to do long term traffic prediction on target roads where only the traffic load of two adjacent roads and certain environmental-contextual factors are monitored. Therefore, the use of graph-based methods is unsuitable in this approach. This study proposes a novel context-aware CNN-GRU-Attention model specifically designed to overcome the limitations of graph-based methods for non-graph structured data. The model combines convolutional layers to capture local dependencies, GRU layers for temporal sequence learning, and a soft attention mechanism to emphasize long-term dependencies within the data. This architecture enables the model to effectively identify complex traffic patterns shaped by contextual factors such as weather conditions and holidays. Experimental evaluations on multiple datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms traditional models, offering notable gains in predictive accuracy and robustness across various forecasting horizons. In summary, this work presents a scalable, adaptable solution to traffic forecasting in scenarios where graph structures are infeasible, advancing the field of urban traffic prediction through a context-sensitive methodology suited for modern traffic management applications.
