articleTitle: Persian Text-Image Retrieval: A Framework Based on Image Captioning and Scalable Vector Search
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Text-image retrieval systems have seen significant advancements with CLIP-based models and Vision-Language models, which rely on vast datasets and powerful computational resources. However, these advancements primarily focus on English and other high-resource languages, leaving a substantial gap for languages like Persian. This paper introduces a pioneering Persian Text-Image Retrieval (PTIR), the first comprehensive framework designed to address Persian's unique challenges. We present three key innovations: (1) a diverse corpus of 1.2 million Persian image-caption pairs from multiple sources; (2) training a vision-language model combining a vision-encoder and a pre-trained Persian text-decoder to optimize cross-modal alignment and generate detailed captions; and (3) a scalable retrieval pipeline using sentence embedding models and vector databases for efficient Persian query-image matching. Evaluations on the Persian-adapted COCO benchmark dataset demonstrate PTIR achieves a 30-40% improvement over existing Persian image captioning models in standard metrics and a 9% mean improvement in Hit@K compared to the CLIP baseline. The framework's modular design enables domain-specific adaptations, offering a blueprint for low-resource language retrieval systems. A subset of our implementation, including code and datasets, is available at: https://rasoulasadiyan.github.io/PTIR.

articleTitle: Predicting Sperm DNA Fragmentation Markers using Basic Semen Parameters and Age: A Preliminary Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Sperm DNA fragmentation is a critical factor in male infertility assessment, often evaluated using tests such as the Sperm Chromatin Structure Assay (SCSA) and the TUNEL assay. Despite their diagnostic importance, these tests are expensive, resource-intensive, and not universally accessible, creating a need for alternative, cost-effective approaches. This study uniquely investigates the feasibility of predicting DNA fragmentation markers using only basic semen parameters and male age. Utilizing a dataset of6,000 patients, we applied a range of regression models, from linear models to tree-based methods and neural network approaches, to predict the continuous values of TUNEL and SCSA. Feature importance analysis of the best-performing model identified the interaction between immotile sperm and male age as the most significant predictor. While the predictive accuracy of these models requires further refinement, this novel approach demonstrates the potential to reduce reliance on expensive testing methods. Our findings lay the foundations for developing accessible risk models, advancing cost-effective diagnostics and clinical decision-making in male infertility assessment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Learning Performance through LLM-Driven Adaptive Contents Based on Facial Engagement Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Recent advancements in AI have opened new avenues for personalized education, enabling learning environments to adapt to individual needs. This study explores the intersection of AI and Image Processing, mainly using facial emotion detection to monitor cognitive engagement and distraction during learning tasks. Previous research highlights the efficacy of emotion detection in identifying cognitive states and improving educational outcomes through personalized learning environments. Our primary goal is to evaluate how AI can adapt educational content in real time to enhance learning effectiveness based on emotional feedback. We utilized an LLM to develop educational content and identified moments of distraction or disengagement by monitoring learners' facial emotions while interacting with the system. Upon detecting distraction, the LLM dynamically restructures the content, subtly reintegrating it into subsequent materials without the learners' awareness. This method reinforces learning by presenting material in varied contexts, thereby improving learners' understanding. Our preliminary results indicate that this approach enhances comprehension levels in distracted learners. Furthermore, integrating emotion-based monitoring with LLMs may provide a responsive educational framework that adapts to learners' immediate needs, promoting deep cognitive engagement and a pleasant personalized learning experience. These findings suggest broader applications beyond academic learning, including professional training. It is the ambition of any learning system to be able to detect any attention fall and to have smart reactions without learners' awareness, which is the vision of our approach.

articleTitle: On Formal Specification of Automated Lane Keeping Systems Requirements
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Automated Lane Keeping Systems (ALKS) are regulated by UNECE Regulation No. 157, which outlines safety and performance requirements for these systems. However, the natural language used in such regulations often contains ambiguities, making it challenging to derive clear, verifiable specifications for validating the behavior of automated driving systems. This study tackles this challenge by presenting a systematic methodology for formalizing regulatory requirements, focusing on temporal constraints. A case study demonstrates the approach, highlighting the process of formalizing and validating requirements using Linear Temporal Logic. By transforming ambiguous regulatory language into precise, machine-verifiable specifications, this work supports certification and homologation processes of automated driving systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing English-Persian Neural Machine Translation with a Large-Scale Parallel Dataset and Relative Position Representations
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Transformer-based models have revolutionized neural machine translation (NMT), particularly with the introduction of the encoder-decoder architecture. However, training these models effectively often requires large amounts of parallel data or pretraining on massive unlabeled corpora. In the context of English-Persian translation, the lack of extensive parallel datasets has hindered progress. To address this, we introduce a new dataset of 4 million English-Persian parallel sentences that span various topics. Without any pretraining on unlabeled data, our model achieves a BLEU score of 47 on the PEPC benchmark and 35 on the MIZAN benchmark, demonstrating strong performance. We used Transformers with relative position representations, enabling the model to generalize to sequence lengths not seen during training. To promote further research and reproducibility, we have open-sourced both the dataset1 and the trained model2, supporting advancements in English-Persian NMT.

articleTitle: LoopGAN: A Novel Multi-Step Generative Architecture for Sequential Stock Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This paper introduces “LoopGAN,” an advanced generative model architecture designed for sequential stock forecasting, leveraging the strengths of Conditional GAN (CGAN) and Least Squares GAN (LSGAN) to enhance prediction accuracy in highly volatile financial time series. LoopGAN's unique recursive prediction mechanism allows each output to feed back as input, creating dynamic, extended forecasts across multiple time steps. Extensive evaluation of the Dow J ones Industrial Average (DJIA) dataset, highlights LoopGAN's superior performance, achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAP E) of 0.005739. This result surpasses traditional models, with LoopGAN outperforming LSTM and RNN models, which registered MAPE scores of 0.006803 and 0.008023, respectively. These findings underscore LoopGAN's robustness, offering a marked improvement in prediction accuracy and confirming its reliability for complex financial forecasting tasks.

articleTitle: Real-Time Collaborative Route Planning in Autonomous Vehicles by Leveraging Optimized Quantum Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: In this paper, we present an approach to enhance the intelligence of autonomous vehicles by focusing on real-time collaborative route planning. This aspect is critical not only for individual vehicles but also for ensuring effective interaction among multiple autonomous systems. The challenge is to optimize route planning algorithms for real-time operation without compromising accuracy. To address this, we leverage quantum computing techniques, integrating them with CNN architectures to develop Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks (QCNNs) and the Optimized QCNN. Neural networks play a key role in tasks such as predicting paths, estimating traffic flow, and selecting optimal routes, ensuring efficient and adaptive planning. The integration of quantum computing with neural networks significantly enhances real-time performance and the Optimized QCNN, developed using the Circuit Depth Reduction strategy, further improves accuracy and convergence rate. Our evaluation, conducted on the Cityscapes Dataset, demonstrates that QCNNs comparing with traditional CNNs achieve faster convergence rate and lower loss value. Furthermore, Optimized QCNNs surpass standard QCNNs in both convergence rate and loss, while also achieving higher accuracy even than traditional CNNs, making them a powerful model for real-time collaborative route planning in autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Irrigation Optimization in Agricultural Fields Using Deep Reinforcement Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: In recent years, due to the world population growth, the demand for agricultural products has also increased. Global crises such as climate change, destruction of water resources, pollution and destruction of aquatic ecosystems, have limited the access to clean water to irrigate the agricultural fields in a global scale. Meanwhile, according to the reports of Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), about 70% of global water consumption is allocated to agricultural activities. Therefore, it is necessary to minimize water consumption during agricultural irrigation while maximizing crop yield by the end of the season. Most IoT frameworks used in irrigation systems collect data from the soil and weather, then send it to the user, leaving the final decision on irrigation to the user. This approach may cause water wastage or even water stress for the plants as the amount of water irrigated in fields may be low. In this paper, we will use deep reinforcement learning approaches to reach this goal. We propose a novel approach to minimize water usage while keeping the yield produced at the highest level. Our approach utilizes DQN and A2C networks. The findings demonstrate that our methods reduce water wastage compared to previous approaches, making it more flexible and practical in varying weather and soil conditions.

articleTitle: iTAG: Easy, Rapid, Automatic Intelligent Tagging for Educational Contents
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: To enhance the effectiveness of Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITSs), providing learners with learning objects (LOs) that meet their educational needs is crucial. This requires comprehensive metadata to evaluate the suitability of LOs for personalized learning. Existing metadata models, such as IEEE Learning Object Metadata (LOM), primarily capture bibliographic details but lack the depth needed to describe pedagogical and educational attributes. This paper introduces an intelligent tagger (iTAG), a lightweight, AI-powered platform designed to annotate educational content with rich metadata automatically. By leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP), machine learning techniques, and domain-specific rules, iTAG automates the extraction of general and pedagogical metadata from text-based LOs. iTAG addresses the limitations of traditional metadata extraction methods by offering higher accuracy, scalability, and resource efficiency, making it suitable for sizeable educational content repositories. The experimental results demonstrate iTAG's ability to accurately generate metadata comparable to expert annotations accurately, achieving 100% precision for basic metadata fields like interactivity type and language and 60-70% accuracy for more complex attributes like semantic density and difficulty. This automatic tagging system offers a practical solution for scaling personalized learning, reducing the dependence on manual metadata annotation while improving the quality of recommendations within ITSs.

articleTitle: Cyber Protection Gap: Challenges and Remedies
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Various challenges including the rapidly evolving cyber threat landscape and uncertainties around the insurability of cyber risks have exposed the growing cyber protection gap, where organizations' cyber risk exposures exceed their available coverage. While cyber economic losses are projected to exceed a few trillion USD, cyber insurance premiums are around a few billion USD only. This paper aims to quantify the cyber protection gap using two methods: analysis of industry data on global cyber insurance uptake, and case studies of high-profile cyber incidents. The study identifies key challenges contributing to the cyber protection gap, including insufficient risk awareness, coverage limitations, and lack of cyber risk modeling capabilities. To address these issues, the paper proposes several remedies. These findings offer valuable insights for organizations, insurers, and policymakers to strengthen organizational cyber resilience and narrow the widening cyber protection gap.

articleTitle: AI-based Malicious Bitcoin Transaction Detection Framework for Real Estate in Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: In recent times, there has been an increase in the use of technologies like Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR). These technologies serve various purposes in the Metaverse. Metaverse is also integrated with blockchain technology and this has lead to various innovative developments in virtual and physical real estate transactions. However, this has also increased the probability of vulnerabilities in these transactions involving Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies. An impersonator pretending to be a genuine buyer may hack into these systems and get access to restricted data. This paper proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based framework for detecting malicious transactions in the metaverse. Our model uses various machine learning (ML) algorithms to classify the transactions into malicious and non-malicious transactions. By incorporating an AI detection mechanism, we aim to reduce the fraudulent transactions in the metaverse. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, showing good performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score when applied to real estate transactions.

articleTitle: GenAtt NIDS Attack: A Practical Generative Adversarial Attack Against Network Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) have made tremendous progress by combining Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques, and they currently perform well against both known and unexpected threats. However, because of intrinsic flaws, adversarial attacks may reduce their detection effectiveness. In this study, an attention-based generative method for developing adversarial assaults utilizing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) is presented. Our approach avoids IDS detection by leveraging attention mechanisms' sequential memory capabilities and producing semantically meaningful modified packets. We address the heterogeneous nature of attack packets with normalized evaluation, enabling meaningful inferences for cybersecurity experts. Using a black-box adversarial attack with Active Learning and request-and-answer queries, we achieved a practical analysis. Compared to prior work showing a 15.3 % drop in IDS detection rates, our method resulted in an 11.3% drop-a slight but considerable reduction-while using only 20 % of the queries. This highlights the efficiency of our approach in reducing anomalous query volumes and maintaining realistic network presence.

articleTitle: Bitcoin Price Forecasting with Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Forecasting bitcoin prices using deep learning techniques has gained significant attention recently. Despite the success of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) across various domains, there is a crucial issue in bitcoin price prediction: the ability to accurately capture correlations between temporal data points. Moreover, GANs face notable inherent challenges, particularly training instability and mode collapse. In this paper, we employ windowing and conditioning techniques to capture correlations between prices and other relevant features such as technical indicators. Additionally, we use a hybrid Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based generator that combines a convolution layer and LSTM to improve learning from temporal data. Appropriate loss functions are also utilized for the discriminator and generator to enhance training stability and mitigate mode collapse. The proposed method was evaluated on the historical Bitcoin data sourced from the Yahoo Finance website. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code for the proposed method is available on GitHub: https://github.com/mahdimanian/draganbtc/

articleTitle: Classification of Imbalanced Data Streams Using Ensemble Learning and Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: While several methods have been proposed to address imbalanced data stream processing and graph-based learning individually, their combination remains an unexplored research area that requires further investigation. This paper proposes a novel ensemble framework that combines Graph Neural Networks (GNN) and boosting techniques to tackle this gap. Furthermore, we used the Graph SMOTE approach to balance the class distribution within the data stream while preserving the graph structure. The experimental findings highlight the proposed method's superior performance over existing approaches, showcasing its capability to address the temporal and structural complexities of imbalanced graph streams while maintaining resilience and adaptability to evolving concept drift. Our framework reflected an improvement in AUC and G-mean metrics when evaluated on a real-world dataset, achieving a 20% increase in classification performance compared to baseline approaches.

articleTitle: MRKG-DSP: Enhanced Multimodal Reasoning with Knowledge Graphs, Dynamic Semantic Pruning and LLM Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to Knowledge Graph (KG) reasoning that integrates and Large Language Models (LLMs) into dynamically pruned message-passing networks. Conventional knowledge graph reasoning methods frequently encounter challenges related to scalability and noise, especially in multi-hop reasoning tasks that engage extensive and intricate graphs. To solve these issues, our approach introduces a novel pruning mechanism that selectively removes irrelevant nodes based on both structural and semantic information. By incorporating Semantic Random Walks with Node2Vec, we enhance node em beddings with contextual semantics derived from pre-trained word embeddings, leading to more informed pruning decisions. Additionally, we leverage the capabilities of LLMs to integrate unstructured textual data into the reasoning process, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of the query context. The proposed methodology not only improves the efficiency of KG reasoning by reducing computational complexity but also enhances accuracy in answering complex queries. Experimental results on benchmark QA datasets, such as CSQA, demonstrate that our approach significantly improves accuracy, achieving 75.10% on test data and 79.69% on development data, while exceeding existing techniques in reasoning effectiveness.

articleTitle: Real-Time Biometric Analysis of Eye Movement Patterns in Human Spatial Navigation
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Human spatial navigation is crucial for daily functioning and cognitive development. It mainly relies on the egocentric and allocentric systems with different developmental trajectories. This study presents a data-driven approach to quantify spatial navigation performance through eye movement pattern analysis. Using the Leiden Navigation Test (LNT) as our experimental framework, we extracted and analyzed multiple eye-tracking metrics to identify distinct visual signatures associated with different navigation strategies. Our correlation analysis revealed significant patterns: landmark recognition tasks demonstrated correlations with blink amplitude and left saccade velocity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r=0.38-0.4,\ p\leq 0.05)$</tex>, while allocentric spatial processing strongly correlated with vertical scanning parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r=0.41-0.5,\ p < 0.05)$</tex>. Most notably, path survey tasks showed robust correlations with left saccade metrics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r=0.62-0.68, p < 0.0001)$</tex> and horizontal eye movement energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r=0.54,\ p < 0.01)$</tex>. Path route tasks exhibited inverse relationships with fixation frequency and saccade duration <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(r=-0.43$</tex> to -0.52, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p < 0.02)$</tex>. These findings establish a quantitative foundation for developing automated assessment tools and potential real-time navigation assistance systems based on eye movement patterns.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models for OCR Post-Processing in Persian: From ParsBERT to GPT
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) refers to the automatic identification of text in images and its conversion into searchable and editable formats. Due to its extensive applications, OCR is considered a crucial and challenging topic in the field of computer vision. In Persian, the unique characteristics of the script often result in OCR outputs with significant errors, which can compromise readability and comprehension of the content, emphasizing the need for error correction, particularly in terms of spelling. This study investigates the performance of four large language models-ParsBERT, LLaMA, Mistral, and GPT-for enhancing OCR outputs. Additionally, an innovative approach that integrates ParsBERT with other models is introduced. These models were evaluated on three corpora of varying sizes and complexities using diverse evaluation metrics, including precision, accuracy, recall, and others. Our comparative analysis highlights the strengths and weaknesses of each model across different scenarios, providing deeper insights into their performance. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approaches outperform standalone models across all corpora, significantly reducing error rates and improving key metrics such as precision, accuracy, and recall.

articleTitle: QIGA: Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithm for Dynamic Scheduling in Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This paper introduces a Quantum-Inspired Genetic Algorithm (QIGA) for efficient scheduling in a Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) environment. Inspired by the principles of quantum computing, it enhances solution diversity and convergence in the MEC landscape with heterogeneous resources and dynamic tasks. In this work, the QIGA framework is applied to an optimization problem with multiple conflicting objectives: makespan, energy consumption, and resource utilization. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, which shows improvement over three state-of-the-art scheduling methods in varied burst MEC scenarios in energy consumption about 15.7% on average and up to 39%, 20.5% in makespan, 27.5% in resource utilization, and latency up to 69.9%.

articleTitle: Point-LN: A Lightweight Framework for Efficient Point Cloud Classification Using Non-Parametric Positional Encoding
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: We introduce Point-LN, a novel lightweight frame-work engineered for efficient 3D point cloud classification. Point-LN integrates essential non-parametric components-such as Farthest Point Sampling (FPS), k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), and non-learnable positional encoding-with a streamlined learnable classifier that significantly enhances classification accuracy while maintaining a minimal parameter footprint. This hybrid architecture ensures low computational costs and rapid inference speeds, making Point-LN ideal for real-time and resource-constrained applications. Comprehensive evaluations on benchmark datasets, including ModelNet40 and ScanObjectNN, demonstrate that Point-LN achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, all while offering exceptional efficiency. These results establish Point-LN as a robust and scalable solution for diverse point cloud classification tasks, highlighting its potential for widespread adoption in various computer vision applications. For more details, see the code at: https://github.com/asalarpour/Point_LN.

articleTitle: Integrating Structural Information: Comparing Classification-Based and Segmentation-Based Predictors in Bioinformatics (Case Study: Protein-Peptide Region Residue-Level Interaction) Using Structural Information
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Understanding the regions where proteins bind to peptides is vital for studying diseases like cancer, as it sheds light on various cellular processes and aids in drug discovery. Although researchers can experimentally investigate protein-peptide interactions at the region level by analyzing the structures of their complexes, only a limited number of these structures are known. Additionally, experiments to determine these interactions can be both costly and time-consuming. Computational methods provide an alternative and complementary approach to experimental techniques. As a result, using computational methods to predict peptide-binding regions can significantly enhance the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of experimental research. To leverage these advantages, this study introduces a new method named Structure-based Prediction of Residue-level Interaction of Peptides (SPRINT-Pep), designed to pinpoint the binding regions between proteins and peptides. This approach leverages two distinct predictive models: a classification-based model combining DeepResNet with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) and a segmentation-based model called DeepU-Net. Our predictions outperform other state-of-the-art methods in terms of F-measures (by at least 23%), precision (by at least 3.7%), and the balance between sensitivity and specificity (by about 7.7%). These findings demonstrate the proficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Low-cost Epicenter Estimation Scheme for Earthquake Early Warning Systems: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach to estimate the epicenter of an earthquake and calculate the Peak Ground Motion (PGA) at the epicenter, using fixed-location smartphone sensors has been proposed. The proposed scheme is a first step in designing a low-cost Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) system. In the proposed method, multiple potential earthquake epicenters are estimated based on the earthquake signals recorded by limited number of fixed-location smartphones. Then, the actual epicenter is estimated and its PGA is calculated. These results can be used to determine possible disaster areas for early warning initiation. Evaluation results on actual earthquake data has resulted in an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 88% in estimating the PGA. The estimated epicenter position is 1.28 and 12.07 kilometers away from the actual ones in the Damavand and Mallard simulated datasets, respectively. Simulations demonstrate the feasibility of using smartphone sensors for real-time earthquake detection, offering an accessible alternative for regions with limited resources, at the cost of slightly reduced precision compared to existing systems that benefit from high precision accelerometers.

articleTitle: Designing a Distributed LLM-Based Search Engine as a Foundation for Agent Discovery
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of decentralized AI-powered Search Engine agents for managing tasks across vari-ous domains. By simulating real-world scenarios, we demonstrate how these agents collaborate within a distributed framework to perform complex tasks efficiently. Central to this system is an AI-powered Search Engine that facilitates seamless matchmaking between agents, allowing them to share expertise and resources. This search engine leverages the power and capabilities of large language models (LLMs), enhancing agent discovery and interaction. The study highlights the multi-level functionality of agents, ranging from basic API interactions to advanced decision-making capabilities. The communication protocols implemented enable smooth agent collaboration and task completion. This work sets the foundation for future advancements in decentralized agent networks, contributing to the development of more sophisticated, equitable, and secure digital ecosystems.

articleTitle: EMA-Affinity: A Statistical Approach for Node Affinity Prediction in Dynamic Graphs
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Dynamic graphs serve as an abstract mathematical model applicable to various real-world scenarios, allowing the integration of complex temporal, structural, and relational patterns in data. To our knowledge, while much of the literature focuses on employing dynamic graph representation learning models for dynamic node classification or link prediction, the task of node affinity prediction-aimed at estimating a node's affinity toward other nodes over time-has shown poor performance with these dynamic graph machine learning models. One of the open challenges in addressing this problem is designing a model that effectively considers the long-term dependencies between nodes for predicting node affinities. In this work, we propose EMA-affinity, a deterministic statistical model that utilizes exponential smoothing to account for long-term correlations between nodes in its predictions, thereby addressing this challenge. We evaluate and visualize EMA-affinity using the TGBN-trade benchmark dataset and demonstrate that it outperforms the current best (implemented) model, i.e. persistent forecast, for node affinity prediction, as measured by Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain, and test the method's robustness. Also, we present an analytic framework for the comparison of different models' performance on different dynamic graph machine learning tasks.

articleTitle: Advanced Stock Market Prediction Using Unsupervised Federated Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: In the realm of stock market prediction, traditional supervised learning approaches often struggle with the vast and diverse nature of financial data, coupled with privacy concerns. This paper explores a novel methodology that combines unsupervised learning techniques with federated learning system to enhance stock market prediction models. We present a comprehensive system where local models, trained using unsupervised methods, contribute to a global model through federated aggregation. By leveraging federated learning, our approach allows multiple financial institutions to collaboratively train models on their decentralized data while preserving data privacy. This approach addresses the challenges of data heterogeneity and communication efficiency, providing a robust and scalable solution for advanced stock market forecasting. Our experiments demonstrate that integrating unsupervised learning with federated learning not only improves predictive accuracy but also enhances the model's ability to identify emerging market trends and anomalies. Finally, we compare our distributed data model with other machine learning models that use local data.

articleTitle: Lymphocyte Segmentation Using Enhanced-YOLO in Histopathological Images of Mycosis Fungoides
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: Mycosis Fungoides (MF), most common cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, is diagnosed by detecting lymphocytes in epidermal region of skin in histopathological images. This study focused on detecting positive lymphocyte in the epidermal layer of the skin in patients diagnosed with MF. To this end, a set of pathology slides was first collected and annotated under the supervision of a pathologist. The YOLO11 model was initially evaluated on a public dataset and demonstrated superior performance compared to other existing models. Based on these results, YOLO11 was then applied to train on our collected dataset to detect lymphocytes within the epidermal region. While YOLO11 demonstrated strong detection capabilities, further refinement was required to enhance its precision and reduce false positives and false negatives, particularly in complex or overlapping regions. To address this, an Attention U-Net was employed as a restoration network, specifically designed to improve the YOLO11 predictions. This combination of YOLO11 for initial detection and Attention U-Net for post-processing allowed for improved localization accuracy, better detection of lymphocytes, and more reliable classification across different tissue regions.

articleTitle: Forecasting S&P 500 Stock Prices using ARIMA Model Estimated by Particle Swarm Optimization Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 29th International Computer Conference, Computer Society of Iran (CSICC)
abstract: In recent years, neural networks have garnered significant attention in portfolio management, particularly for forecasting stock prices, which is a challenging yet crucial task for the financial market. This study focuses on the S&P 500, a benchmark index that comprises 500 major stocks and serves as a key indicator of the U.S. economy's health. For passive investors, the S&P 500 represents an essential exposure to the U.S. market through index funds. The research addresses the need for accurate stock price predictions by investigating the effectiveness of deep learning models in this domain. In this study, we introduce an innovative approach that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model, creating a hybrid PSO-ARIMA framework designed to improve stock price forecasting accuracy. Through rigorous comparative analysis, the predictive capabilities of the PSO-ARIMA model are evaluated alongside popular models like GRU, LSTM, and traditional ARIMA. Results indicate that the PSO-ARIMA model outperforms these models across all evaluation metrics, including Mean Squared Error (MSE), achieving an MSE of 170.766, highlighting its superior precision and efficiency. The PSO-ARIMA model's effectiveness stems from its ability to leverage the strengths of both ARIMA and PSO-ARIMA models are well-suited for capturing linear trends in time series data, but they often struggle with complex, non-linear patterns common in stock price movements. By integrating PSO, a metaheuristic optimization technique, the model can optimize ARIMA's parameters to better fit the non-linear characteristics of financial data.
